chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not eat while leaning, from the time Allah Mighty and Majestic sent him until He took his soul, out of humility for Allah Mighty and Majestic, and he never had his two knees seen in front of his companion in any gathering.
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never shook hands with a man and then pulled his hand away until the man himself pulled his hand away.
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never repelled an evil deed with an evil deed.
Allah the Exalted said to him: 'Repel evil by what is best.'

And he never denied a beggar at all; if he had it with him, he gave it, or else he said: 'Allah will bring it.' And he did not give anything on the authority of Allah Mighty and Majestic except that Allah authorized it for him; if it were Paradise, Allah Mighty and Majestic would authorize it for him.
He said: And his brother after him, by the One who took his soul, did not eat anything prohibited from the world until he exited from it.
By Allah, if two matters were presented to him, both of which were obedience to Allah Mighty and Majestic, he would take the one that was more difficult upon his body.
By Allah, he freed a thousand slaves for the sake of Allah Mighty and Majestic, from the work of his own hands.
By Allah, no one else could endure the deeds of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) after him, apart from him.
By Allah, no difficulty ever descended upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) except that he placed him in it first, as a reliable one from him for it.

And whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent him with his flag, Jibraeel would fight on his right and Mikaeel on his left. Then he would not return until Allah Mighty and Majestic granted him victory.
ai.seo_question: What were the unique characteristics of the Prophet's humility and Ali ibn Abi Talib's devotion according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) profound humility (tawadu') and gentle character (khuluq), specifically noting his avoidance of eating while reclining and his patience in handshakes. It further elevates Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) as the most capable successor in enduring hardship for God’s sake, highlighting his emancipation of a thousand slaves and his status as the Prophet’s trusted lieutenant in battles accompanied by angels.
